issues.legal_issue: A dispute over whether rent arrears were paid or adjusted does not require provisional rent fixation when the rate of rent is admitted.
material_facts: The tenant admitted the monthly rent rate but disputed owing arrears, claiming that the rent had been paid.
The lower courts found that the receipts offered to prove payment were forged and that rent for the disputed period remained unpaid.
issues.conclusion: A dispute about whether admitted-rate rent was paid or adjusted is not a dispute requiring provisional rent fixation; it must be resolved at trial.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 13(2) of the Madhya Pradesh Accommodation Control Act, 1961, provisional rent is fixed where the dispute concerns the rate of rent, such as when no rate is agreed or the parties assert different rates. A dispute about arrears that turns on alleged payment or adjustment, with the rate admitted, is outside that summary procedure. The Court rejected the broader approaches in Firm Ganeshram Harvilas v. Ramachandra Rao, Jivrambhai v. Amarsingh, the Full Bench ruling discussed in Chhogalal Jankilal v. Idol of Bhagwan Shri Satyanaraya, and Anandilal v. Shiv Dayal Pandey.

predicates.rent_default_eviction_case: The proceeding seeks eviction of a tenant on the ground that rent was not paid after demand.
predicates.rent_rate_admitted: The tenant accepts the agreed rate of rent for the accommodation.
predicates.arrears_dispute_based_on_payment_or_adju: The tenant disputes the arrears by asserting that rent was paid or adjusted, rather than disputing the rate of rent.

issues.definition: When an eviction proceeding concerns rent default, the tenant accepts the rent rate, and the arrears dispute concerns payment or adjustment, provisional rent fixation is not required.

issues.legal_issue: A dispute confined to whether rent at an admitted rate was paid does not suspend the tenant’s continuing obligation to pay or deposit rent during the proceeding.
material_facts: The tenant admitted the monthly rent rate of Rs.60 but claimed to have paid the arrears.
The courts found that rent for the disputed months had not been paid.
The tenant did not comply with the required rent-payment or deposit obligations, and the trial court fixed provisional rent at the admitted rate.
issues.conclusion: The tenant’s obligation to pay or deposit rent for later periods remains operative even when the tenant disputes whether earlier rent was paid; the obligations for different periods are independent.
issues.legal_principle: Section 13(1) imposes separate obligations to pay or deposit rent for the default period and subsequent period, and to continue paying or depositing rent month by month during the proceeding. The word “thereafter” indicates sequence, not dependence between those obligations. Section 13(2) suspends operation of Section 13(1) pending provisional fixation only where the dispute about the amount payable depends on the rate of rent. The Court rejected the contrary interpretation in Jivrambhai v. Amarsingh and Anandilal v. Shiv Dayal Pandey.

predicates.rent_default_eviction_case: The proceeding seeks eviction of a tenant on the ground that rent was not paid after demand.
predicates.rent_rate_admitted: The tenant accepts the agreed rate of rent for the accommodation.
predicates.arrears_dispute_based_on_payment_or_adju: The tenant disputes the arrears by asserting that rent was paid or adjusted, rather than disputing the rate of rent.

issues.definition: In an eviction proceeding, when the tenant accepts the rent rate but disputes arrears on payment or adjustment grounds, the tenant remains obliged to pay or deposit rent for later periods.

issues.legal_issue: A tenant who fails to establish an asserted payment of arrears and does not comply with the applicable rent-payment obligations is not protected from eviction for rent default.
material_facts: The landlords sought eviction for non-payment of rent after serving a demand notice.
The tenant admitted the rent rate and claimed to have paid the rent for the disputed period.
The trial court found the payment receipts forged and found that the rent remained unpaid; the appellate court affirmed those findings.
The trial court fixed provisional rent at the admitted rate, and the tenant did not comply with the applicable payment or deposit obligations.
issues.conclusion: The tenant was not entitled to protection against eviction under Section 12(3) read with Section 13(5); the eviction decree on the rent-default ground was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Section 12(1)(a) permits an eviction suit where legally recoverable arrears are not paid or tendered within the prescribed period after demand. Under Section 12(3), read with Sections 13(1), 13(2) and 13(5), a tenant obtains protection against eviction for rent default by making the required payment or deposit. Where the rate is admitted, the tenant disputes arrears by claiming payment, and that claim fails at trial, Section 13(2) does not provide a basis for suspending the payment obligations. Section 13(6) also permits the court to strike out the defence for non-compliance. The Court disapproved the contrary approach in Anandilal v. Shiv Dayal Pandey.

issues.definition: When an eviction proceeding is based on rent default, the tenant accepts the rent rate, the claimed payment is not proved, and required rent is not paid or deposited, eviction for rent default is permitted.
